title: Telecommunications Amendment (Guaranteeing Mobile Phone Service in Bushfire Zones) Bill 2017
short_title: Telecommunications Amendment (Guaranteeing Mobile Phone Service in Bushfire Zones) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require telecommunications standards for carriers owning or operating critical mobile base stations in bushfire risk areas to maintain standby power capability.
The Australian Communications and Media Authority would set a standard requiring at least 24 hours of standby power at all times for the covered stations.
Emergency Management Australia would identify high-risk communities using relevant state and territory planning laws, with the bill commencing on Royal Assent and standards to follow.
changes: Industry codes and standards could expressly address standby power for mobile base stations in high-risk communities.
The authority would have to consult representative telecommunications bodies before determining the standards.
Standards would be determined by legislative instrument as soon as practicable after commencement.
Exercise of the new power would need to address public interests without undue industry financial or administrative burdens.
summary.affected: Telecommunications carriers, residents of identified bushfire risk communities and the responsible Commonwealth agencies would be affected.
